items.followUp: State the Associative Law of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: Checks the defining idea of commutativity.
rubric.description: States that changing the order of operands does not change the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both the change in order and unchanged result are stated.

rubric.why: Checks the Boolean identities for OR and AND.
rubric.description: Gives the commutative identities for both OR and AND.

modelAnswer: In the commutative law, changing the order of the operands does not change the result.
For Boolean algebra: A + B = B + A and A · B = B · A.

rubric.why: Checks that topology describes a network layout.
rubric.description: Identifies topology as the arrangement of devices in a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the arrangement of network devices.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition includes how devices are linked.
rubric.description: Explains that topology describes how devices are connected by communication links.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the connections through communication links.

modelAnswer: Topology is the physical or logical arrangement of devices in a computer network.
It describes how the devices and their communication links are connected.

rubric.why: Checks the endpoints in a point-to-point connection.
rubric.description: States that it provides a direct connection between two devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the direct connection and its two endpoints.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of the connection.
rubric.description: States that the link is dedicated to communication between the two devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the dedicated-link idea.

modelAnswer: A point-to-point connection provides a direct connection between two devices.
The link is dedicated to communication between those two devices.

items.followUp: Describe star and mesh network topologies.

rubric.why: Checks the main structure of bus topology.
rubric.description: States that all devices connect to one main cable or backbone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the shared main-cable arrangement.

rubric.why: Checks how the bus cable is used.
rubric.description: States that data travels along the shared cable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining data transmission along the shared bus cable.

rubric.why: Checks the connections and shape of ring topology.
rubric.description: States that devices connect to neighbouring devices to form a closed loop.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both the neighbour connections and loop arrangement.

rubric.why: Checks how data moves in a ring topology.
rubric.description: States that data travels from one device to the next around the ring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the device-to-device data movement around the ring.

modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all devices are connected to one main cable called the bus or backbone.
Data travels along this shared cable to the connected devices.
In a ring topology, each device is connected to its neighbouring device(s), forming a closed loop.
Data travels from one device to the next around the ring.
